notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates ring occupancy, receive fairness, transmit reclamation, memory ownership, metadata validity, device capability and queue capacity.

evidence: Executed five receive completions and two transmit completions with receive budget three.
Confirmed the first poll reclaims two TX completions and processes three RX packets without completion, while the second processes two RX packets and permits rearm.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic computation validates separate receive-budget and transmit-reclamation accounting only; it implements no NAPI, interrupt race, descriptor, DMA, driver, NIC or packet.

evidence: Re-derived safe modular ring occupancy and the bound that receive work never exceeds the NAPI budget.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed receive and transmit as paired ownership pipelines spanning descriptors, DMA, NAPI, XDP, SKBs, protocols, qdiscs, offloads, completion, overload and teardown.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed current Linux networking mechanisms as implementable concerns, including race-safe NAPI completion, page recycling, offload fallback, queue stop/wake, staged drop localization and reset containment. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from device queues and receive processing through protocol delivery and the reverse transmit path, then overload, observation and testing, followed by twelve obligations, sixteen trade-offs, twenty-five misconceptions, ten examples and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external operating-systems academic, Linux networking, network-driver, NIC-vendor, protocol, XDP, performance, security, independent-verification or certification review is claimed.
